protocol.py: 6 biology problems (1 error, 2 warnings, 3 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 47 stocks
   line 110:  p20.aspirate(2, rack[src_well])
   At line 110 the tip went into template 2 (tube A2 in slot 2), template 3 (tube A3 in slot
   2), template 4 (tube A4 in slot 2), template 5 (tube A5 in slot 2) and 43 more while it
   still carried buffer (tube A1 in slot 1), dntp (tube A2 in slot 1), polymerase (tube A3
   in slot 1), fwd primer (tube A4 in slot 1) and 49 more from an earlier step (this line
   did it 47 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next
   liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid
   drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 47 other wells: wells A2, A3,
   A4, A5, A6, B1, B2, B3 and 39 more in slot 4.
   Affected: tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2, B3 and 15 more in slot 2; tubes A1, A2, A3,
   A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 3.
   Also reached 47 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2, B3 and 39 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 110 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [a2bea5009fbf]

2. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
   line 82:  p20.dispense(take, mm_tube)
   At line 82 the robot put polymerase into tube B1 in slot 1. Take tube B1 in slot 1: at
   that moment it held 290.4 ul, only 264 ul of it water or buffer, and the water came
   afterwards, at line 77, to make the 1042.8 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built
   on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a
   reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution.
   Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a
   restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts
   on mis-primed template.
   Affected: tube B1 in slot 1.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to tube B1 in slot 1: water and buffer first, then the sample,
   then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix
   it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [7b7a4a0ecc91]

3. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 48 wells: 2 × 20 ul in 23 ul
   line 100:  p300.mix(2, 20, plate[well])
   At line 100 the tip mixes wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4 with
   2 strokes of 20 ul in a well holding 23 ul (this line did it 48 times). 2 strokes of 20
   ul move 1.74 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the
   mixing work). Fewer than 3 strokes do not mix a well. Integra draws over 80% of the well
   five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not
   at the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits
   the error.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (18.4 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 18.4,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [c7235596e02e]

4. NOTE WELL-CAPACITY: Declared more than the well holds: 2000 ul in a 1898 ul well, 1 well
   line 76:  p300.aspirate(take, src)
   At line 76 the robot draws from tube A6 in slot 1, which the protocol declares (line 43)
   to hold 2000 ul; the well holds 1897.79 ul. The prep sheet cannot be followed as written.
   Wells: tube A6 in slot 1.
   Affected: tube A6 in slot 1.
   Fix: Declare what the well can really hold, or use a bigger container.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [e50fc9dd1428]

5. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 48 wells of dntp and polymerase with a
sample
   line 99:  p300.dispense(23.0, plate[well])
   At line 99 the robot starts putting dntp and polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL
   PCR Full Skirt (slot 4), and 48 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on
   this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a
   reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal
   and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5,
   A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.75 ul of dntp and polymerase and 2 ul of water
   in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [e0a0923b6d1d]

6. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 48 wells never mixed after template 1, template 2, template 3,
template 4 and 44 more went in (8% of the well)
   line 111:  p20.dispense(2, plate[well])
   At line 111 the robot added template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 44 more to
   wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4, which already held buffer,
   dntp, polymerase, fwd primer and 2 more (this line did it 48 times). The addition was 8%
   of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two
   liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before
   cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4 after line 111:
   `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [0c64b159e5df]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: 47 stocks
findings.explanation: At line 110 the tip went into template 2 (tube A2 in slot 2), template 3 (tube A3 in slot 2), template 4 (tube A4 in slot 2), template 5 (tube A5 in slot 2) and 43 more while it still carried buffer (tube A1 in slot 1), dntp (tube A2 in slot 1), polymerase (tube A3 in slot 1), fwd primer (tube A4 in slot 1) and 49 more from an earlier step (this line did it 47 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 47 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2, B3 and 39 more in slot 4.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 110 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
findings.explanation: At line 82 the robot put polymerase into tube B1 in slot 1. Take tube B1 in slot 1: at that moment it held 290.4 ul, only 264 ul of it water or buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 77, to make the 1042.8 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to tube B1 in slot 1: water and buffer first, then the sample, then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: Mixing too weak to stir 48 wells: 2 × 20 ul in 23 ul
findings.explanation: At line 100 the tip mixes wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4 with 2 strokes of 20 ul in a well holding 23 ul (this line did it 48 times). 2 strokes of 20 ul move 1.74 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing work). Fewer than 3 strokes do not mix a well. Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
findings.fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (18.4 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 18.4, well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.

findings.title: Declared more than the well holds: 2000 ul in a 1898 ul well, 1 well
findings.explanation: At line 76 the robot draws from tube A6 in slot 1, which the protocol declares (line 43) to hold 2000 ul; the well holds 1897.79 ul. The prep sheet cannot be followed as written. Wells: tube A6 in slot 1.
findings.fix: Declare what the well can really hold, or use a bigger container.

findings.title: No no-template control: 48 wells of dntp and polymerase with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 99 the robot starts putting dntp and polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 4), and 48 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.75 ul of dntp and polymerase and 2 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 48 wells never mixed after template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 44 more went in (8% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 111 the robot added template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 44 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4, which already held buffer, dntp, polymerase, fwd primer and 2 more (this line did it 48 times). The addition was 8% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 40 more in slot 4 after line 111: `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
